survivors.target: hr-skradin-town-beach (D1 ★) + hr-krka boardwalk
survivors.proposal: Add Primošten / Mala Raduča (hr-primosten-mala-raduca, already in the pool, rated 4) as the D1 swim highlight, sitting directly on the coastal Zadar→Split line (~58km/45min from the Split ćevapi, near-zero detour off the A1). Make the D1 swim a fork: EITHER do the Krka boardwalk + included boat down + the modest Skradin town beach (EUR40pp/~EUR160 for 4), OR skip the Krka ticket entirely and make Primošten the relaxed arrival swim. Re-star whichever the group picks that morning.
survivors.rationale: The day's committed ★ is the swim, but Skradin town beach is self-described as 'modest in size... a town beach,' and the swim only exists because they bought the EUR40pp Krka boardwalk ticket (swimming is BANNED at Skradinski Buk). For a group that dislikes sightseeing boardwalks and loves real swims/coves, EUR160 for a no-swim walk + a small town beach is the weakest value block on D1. Primošten is a postcard turquoise pebble beach (rated 4), genuinely better water, on-route, and free — giving the group a clean way to drop the EUR160 boardwalk on a hot, jet-lagged arrival day without losing a swim. The note itself already flags Krka as 'THE skip candidate.'
survivors.tradeoff: Skipping Krka loses the famous Skradinski Buk cascade view (the only iconic sight on the otherwise transit-heavy D1) and the novelty boat ride. Primošten is a busier town beach, not a wild cove, and gets crowded midday — so this is a swap of 'iconic-but-passive-and-pricey' for 'pretty-and-free-but-ordinary.' Keep both pinned and decide on the day by energy/budget; this is purely additive, not a forced removal.

survivors.target: D1 morning water block (replacing/augmenting the passive Krka boardwalk)
survivors.proposal: Pin the Zrmanja swim options as a conditional D1 alternative: Berberov buk swimming waterfall (hr-berberov-buk, rated 4 — free tufa pools you can actually swim/jump in) and/or the Zrmanja self-rent kayak (hr-zrmanja-selfrent-kayak, Raftrek). These reachable off the A1 Maslenica/Obrovac exit. Frame as: if the group wants an ACTIVE self-rent/swim highlight over a EUR40pp walk, take the Zrmanja inland line instead of Krka.
survivors.rationale: This is the group's exact taste — free, swimmable, self-rent, hidden-gem water — versus Krka's pay-to-walk, no-swim boardwalk. Berberov buk is rated 4 with Croatian guides calling it 'one of the most beautiful waterfalls in Croatia... suitable for swimming,' and the self-rent kayak needs no guide/licence. It would make D1 an activity day rather than a sightseeing day.
survivors.tradeoff: HONEST DOWNSIDE — this is why it stays a conditional option, not the default: Zrmanja/Berberov sit NORTH and inland of the airport (~48km up, then a long inland-to-coast leg to Split), so routing airport→Zrmanja→Split is ~16km+ longer straight-line than airport→Krka→Split AND off the fast A1, adding real driving on the tight 10:00-start arrival day. It trades the efficient coastal spine for a better activity. Only worth it if the group is fresh and wants to lead D1 with water; otherwise the coastal Krka/Primošten line is faster to the Krvavica camp.

survivors.target: Day 2 morning (06:00-11:00), on the Krvavica -> Brela -> Zadvarje line. Pull hr-punta-rata (43.37,16.9228) ± hr-vruja-spring-beach (43.3733,16.9397)
survivors.proposal: Add a Brela morning swim block to fill the hollow pre-canyoning slot: Punta Rata at ~07:00-08:30 (before the parasol crush, free shingle, sea ~20-22C), with the option to walk 2km north to the Vruja submarine freshwater spring for a snorkel over the upwelling vent. Brela is directly on the road from camp to the Zadvarje canyoning meet, so this is zero detour. Leave by ~09:30 to make a late-morning/midday canyoning slot.
survivors.rationale: On a Wednesday the verified weekday Biokovo closure (07:00-15:00) very likely blocks the planned summit, leaving 06:00-11:00 with nothing committed and the day resting on a single anchor (canyoning). Punta Rata is one of Europe's top-ranked beaches and sits exactly on the camp->Zadvarje path; the morning pre-09:00 window is precisely when it's good. It converts dead time into a low-cost coast highlight on a 2-night base with no drive pressure.
survivors.tradeoff: It is a swim, and D1's highlight is already a Krka/Skradin swim - so this is back-to-back water in the broad sense. Mitigant: canyoning (cold gorge + jumps + 55m rappel) remains D2's distinct headline, and a static beach swim reads as slack-filler, not a repeated highlight activity. Still, if the group wants morning variety over a beach, the Gubavica falls add (below) is the alternative.

vet.target: Day 2 morning (Wed Jun 17) — add a Brela / Punta Rata pre-canyoning swim block on the Krvavica → Zadvarje line
vet.reasoning:
Strongest case to KEEP CURRENT: (1) Back-to-back/triple water — D1's highlight is the Krka/Skradin swim and D2's anchor is Cetina canyoning (a water activity), so wedging a beach swim between them looks like three water touches in two days, brushing the no-back-to-back-activity rule. (2) Rest-buffer erosion — the user explicitly protects slack; a 07:00 beach alarm PLUS ~3h cold-gorge canyoning on a 2-night base could turn a recoverable morning into a tiring one. (3) The day does NOT need it — it already satisfies the one-highlight-per-day rule via canyoning, so nothing is failing.

Why the change still wins anyway: The hollow-morning premise is VERIFIED, not hypothetical — the plan's own data (hr-biokovo-tollroad bestTime, committed last commit) records a weekday 07:00–15:00 Biokovo road closure in effect until Jun 19 2026, and D2 = Wed Jun 17 sits inside it, so the summit is genuinely off and 06:00–11:00 is uncommitted. An empty morning at a campsite is dead time, not rest; a pre-09:00 beach swim is itself low-effort/restful and is exactly heat-optimal under the plan's own AM-water sequencing. It is a droppable slack-filler (the user's preferred shape: options, not a maxed committed day), not a repeated headline — a passive shingle swim is categorically different from a 55m-rappel/12m-jump canyon, so the no-back-to-back rule isn't really tripped. Geography checks out as near-zero detour: Camp Krvavica (43.323,16.986) → Punta Rata (43.370,16.923) is ~10min straight up the coast road you must drive anyway, then turn inland for Zadvarje (43.432,16.891); leave by 09:30 comfortably makes a ~10:00–11:00 canyoning meet. Both pins already exist (hr-punta-rata shortlist, hr-vruja-spring-beach), so this is a plan-attach, not new data.

The MODIFICATION (why not a clean adopt): The Vruja half should NOT be a morning option. The data itself states Vruja has 'No road access: reach by a 2km coastal path north from Punta Rata' with 'no facilities, no shade' — a 2km-each-way walk + snorkel is ~1.5–2h that directly fights the leave-by-09:30 constraint and manufactures the exact time pressure the pressure-free 2-night base avoids. Adopt Punta Rata as the D2 morning swim block; demote Vruja to a footnote usable only if canyoning is dropped or the afternoon runs slow (its own bestTime already says 'afternoon after Punta Rata'). Keep canyoning as the undisputed D2 anchor.
vet.modifiedProposal: Add hr-punta-rata as the D2 morning swim block (~07:00–08:30 at Brela's Punta Rata: free shingle at the water's edge, pre-parasol-crush, sea ~20–22C), leaving by ~09:30 to make a late-morning/midday Cetina canyoning slot (Zadvarje is ~25–30min inland). Frame it explicitly as droppable slack-filler, NOT a second highlight, so canyoning stays the day's headline. survivors.target: Day 3 morning — insert hr-kobas-bay after Walls of Ston (between Ston walls/oysters and the ~13:00 airport-prep departure)
survivors.proposal: After the Ston walls climb + Mali Ston oysters (done by ~10:30), drive ~10-15 min to Kobaš bay (id hr-kobas-bay, 42.8025/17.7428) for a 10:45-12:00 swim and shade cool-off, then leave Pelješac by ~12:15. The new Broce->Kobaš road (paved, built recently) puts this secluded sandy cove on the Ston channel within reach by car; Pržina beyond it stays unpaved and is skipped.
survivors.rationale: D3 is an airport/ferry day whose only nature highlight is the hot, no-shade Ston wall climb — and the group's #1 taste is self-rent water/hidden coves, not limestone walls. The 08:30-13:00 window has 45-75 min of genuine slack after the walls. Kobaš is a clear, calm, pine-shaded cove ~5.5 km off Ston (essentially on-route, no real detour), so a cool-off swim slots in right after the brutal climb with zero risk to the 17:20 pickup or the 20:30 SPOF ferry. It also makes the day's activity profile a swim (distinct from D2 canyoning and D4 kayak), satisfying the >=1-big-highlight rule with the group's preferred activity type.
survivors.tradeoff: Adds ~1h15 + ~25 min round-trip driving to a day that already has a fragile evening; if the morning runs late (Ston gates slip, oyster queue, slow traffic) the swim is the first thing to drop. The access road is winding/narrow (slow last 5 km). Pure-swim value only — no facilities, bring everything.

survivors.target: hr-bacina-jezera (Baćina lakes), Day 3 dayOrder 0.5
survivors.proposal: Drop Baćina lakes from Day 3. Its note assumes an 'afternoon swim break on the drive south', but on D3 there is no afternoon southbound drive: Baćina sits ~30 min NORTH of the Pelješac bridge, so it's passed ~07:30-07:45 while racing to make the 08:30 Ston gate — too early and too cold to swim, and stopping there pushes the ★ Ston slot into the heat/buses. Keep it as a candidate option for a future northbound day, not committed on D3.
survivors.rationale: It's an internally-contradictory stop on this specific day: a swim spot that can only be reached before the day's first activity, at an hour no one swims, on the trip's most time-fragile day. Removing it tightens the morning around the real anchor (Ston 08:30) and frees the swim slot for the on-route Kobaš cove (proposal 1), which is both a better swim and correctly timed (post-climb, ~11:00, warm).
survivors.tradeoff: Loses a freshwater-vs-Adriatic novelty and a quiet leg-stretch; if the group instead leaves Makarska very early and wants a pre-Ston dip, Baćina is the only freshwater option here. Mitigated by keeping it as a candidate, not deleting it from the pool.

survivors.target: Počitelj (ba-pocitelj), D4 late-afternoon stop
survivors.proposal: Drop the Počitelj detour and instead end the day with a Bregava-river swim/waterfall stop at the Stolac bed: pull ba-vodopad-pjene-stolac (Vodopad Pjene, 43.0903/17.9651, ~7km / 12min from the Poplat bed). Drive Kravica → Stolac direct (~24km/47min, no detour), check in, then walk down to the Pjene/Provalije Bregava cascades for a quiet late-afternoon swim. Počitelj can stay in the pool as a 30-min photo option only if someone insists.
survivors.rationale: Počitelj is exactly the stop this group dislikes — an Ottoman old-town/'bare stone hill, little shade,' already shrunk to 45-50min, sold as a sightseeing tick. It's also a genuine detour: Kravica→Stolac is direct (~47min), but Počitelj sits NW toward Čapljina/Mostar (Kravica→Počitelj 24min, then a ~40min backtrack SE to the Stolac bed), so it costs ~30-40min of net driving for a low-taste payoff. The Bregava cascades (Pjene/Provalije) are a hidden, uncrowded, swimmable river-waterfall literally at the bed — nature + a swim + zero extra driving, which is squarely this group's taste and adds real evening slack on a long ferry+drive day. Locals/blogs describe Pjene as a quiet swim spot 'without bumping into too many people.'
survivors.tradeoff: You lose Bosnia's most photogenic Ottoman hill-town (UNESCO-tentative) and a 5-min fig/pomegranate-stall grab. It also stacks a third swim onto a water-heavy day (Mljet AM + Kravica PM + Bregava eve) — but the Bregava stop is optional bed-side slack, not a committed highlight, and June flow can be low/shallow so treat it as a cooling dip, not a waterfall spectacle. If the group actually wants a cultural beat near the bed, Stolac's own Bregava watermills / Radimlja stećci are closer and on-route than Počitelj.

survivors.target: Self-rent kayak/SUP on the Mljet salt lakes (hr-mljet-kayak-sup-selfrent-lakes), D4 ★ morning
survivors.proposal: Flip the morning's lead: make the free Odysseus Cave (hr-odysseus-cave, 1.3km from the Mungos camp) the primary ★ morning activity, and demote the Mali Most salt-lakes kayak to a conditional option ('only if the camp host pre-arranges an early kayak the night before AND you accept the €100-120 NP fee for a ~60-min paddle'). Keep the 12:00 Sobra ferry as the hard anchor either way.
survivors.rationale: The kayak ★ is squeezed and expensive against the 12:00 ferry. Geography: the Mungos camp is at Babino Polje (central), but the kayak is at Mali Most/Pomena — ~25min drive NW + a 10-20min walk in. The Mali Most rental opens 09:00 (earlier only 'if you ask in advance'), and you must drive Pomena→Sobra (~30min) to queue by ~10:45 — so the realistic on-water window is only ~45-60min, for a 4×€25-30 = €100-120 NP entry. Odysseus Cave is 1.3km from camp, free, open all day, and delivers the cliff-jump + sea-cave swim this group rates higher than a paid lake paddle — and they already get genuine self-rent paddling on D7 (Piva), D9 (Skadar river ★) and D10 (Beška/SUP), so a rushed Mljet NP paddle is the most redundant water of the trip.
survivors.tradeoff: You give up the emerald salt-lakes + St Mary islet, which is Mljet's signature scene and arguably prettier than the cave. If the host CAN pre-arrange an ~08:00 kayak and the group is willing to pay the NP fee, the kayak is still the more 'iconic Mljet' choice — so this is a judgment call, not a clear win. Either way it's one-or-the-other (you can't do both and make the ferry).

survivors.target: Blagaj Tekija (ba-blagaj) — currently dayOrder 0, first stop of Day 5
survivors.proposal: Move the whole Blagaj block (Tekija ba-blagaj, Vrelo trout ba-blagaj-trout-terraces, Buna swim ba-buna-blagaj-swim) to AFTER the Mostar core (jump + bridge + Tima-Irma), so the day runs Stolac -> Mostar cool-morning block -> Blagaj midday heat-relief block -> Fortica -> Drežnica -> Ravna. Set Blagaj Tekija's order to ~3.5 (just after Tima-Irma), not 0.
survivors.rationale: Every note on the day already prescribes this: 'cool-morning Mostar block, THEN Blagaj 12km south as the midday heat-relief.' But the committed dayOrder lists Blagaj Tekija first (order 0), which would route the group 12 km south to Blagaj at dawn, back north to Mostar for the 09:00 jump, then south AGAIN for the trout+swim — a double out-and-back. Reordering to Mostar-first matches the notes and kills the backtrack.
survivors.tradeoff: None of substance — it's the sequence the notes already intend. Only caveat: if the route builder already sorts by the bestTime clock rather than dayOrder, this is cosmetic. Worth fixing the field regardless so the displayed order isn't misleading.

survivors.target: Skip-candidate priority: Buna swim (ba-buna-blagaj-swim) vs Fortica (ba-fortica-mostar)
survivors.proposal: Re-label the day's skip candidate: when trimming for time/energy, drop the Buna River swim FIRST and protect Fortica, rather than the current note which flags Fortica as 'the day's slack/skip candidate.' Keep Buna only if the group still wants a quick cold dip right by the trout terraces.
survivors.rationale: D5 already stacks three cold-water immersions — the Stari Most jump, the Buna swim, and the ★ Drežnica canyon — and TWO of them are cliff-jumps (Stari Most + Drežnica's Stupina pool, literally the spot where divers trained for the bridge). That violates the 'no same activity back-to-back/within a day' taste rule and makes the Buna swim the redundant one (a plain cold dip sandwiched between two stronger water items). Fortica is the day's ONLY non-water highlight (skywalk + zipline = land/air variety) and a heat-tolerant late-afternoon fit. Protecting Fortica preserves the one-big-highlight-per-day variety; dropping Buna loses little.
survivors.tradeoff: You lose a 20-min icy swim that's pleasantly placed right after the Buna trout lunch as midday heat-relief. If the day is hot and the group is fine with three water items, keeping Buna is harmless — this is about which item to shed FIRST when tired, not a forced cut.

survivors.target: Day 6 morning (start of day, at the N5 Ravna/Jablanica bed) — pull ba-jablanica-kayak-neretva from the pool
survivors.proposal: Lead Day 6 with the Jablanica Kayak Safari (ba-jablanica-kayak-neretva) instead of opening on the WWII museum. It is a self-guided emerald-Neretva-canyon kayak (~5min / 3.3km from the N5 Ravna Camping bed, ~€25pp, life jackets + waterproof bags + return tow, optional Red Bull cliff-diver rocks to jump from), shortlist + rating-5, on-route, no pre-booking needed in June. This gives the morning a real self-rent-water highlight (exactly the group's taste) on a day whose only current ★ is a city they dislike. One hitch: the operator opens 10:00, so it sets a relaxed-Sunday pace — paddle ~10:00-11:30, then drive Konjic→Sarajevo (~1h) for the afternoon city block, which still lands them in Baščaršija comfortably before the Žuta Tabija sunset (20:32).
survivors.rationale: Day 6 is the weakest day against the hard taste profile: its lone ★ is an old-town city (anti-taste, kept only for vibe), and the morning is a passive WWII museum + a detour lake swim. The day clock is 16h (8.0-24.0) but only ~1h is unavoidable driving, so there is huge slack for a genuine activity. This kayak is the single best on-corridor pull — it sits at the doorstep of the night-5 bed, costs zero net driving, and is precisely the self-rent water + cliff-jump the group loves. It satisfies the #1 rule (a big activity highlight every day) for the day that most lacks one.
survivors.tradeoff: Opens at 10:00, so no dawn start — but the direct Jablanica→Sarajevo drive is short, so the afternoon city/sunset/nightlife plan is unaffected. Mild same-activity flag: D7 is Tara whitewater rafting, so this is paddling on consecutive days — but flat self-rent kayak vs guided whitewater raft are different enough experiences (and different rivers) that it does not read as repetitive.

survivors.target: ba-jablanica-neretva-museum (Battle of Neretva Museum & sunken bridge), Day 6 dayOrder -2.0
survivors.proposal: Drop the Jablanica WWII museum from the committed flow (keep it as a drive-by-only photo of the sunken bridge from the M-17, which costs zero time). It is a passive war museum/monument — the exact 'museums/monuments unless iconic' category the group dislikes — and it currently eats the prime morning window that the Jablanica kayak should own. If the museum stays, it becomes a 30-45min anti-taste sit that delays the 10:00 kayak slot.
survivors.rationale: The group's hard taste rule deprioritizes museums and monuments; this one is neither iconic-enough nor activity-shaped. Removing it frees the morning for the on-route kayak (proposal 1) and trims a low-value stop, which the plan's slack philosophy explicitly rewards (every day should survive dropping an item). The sunken bridge is still visible for free from the road as they leave Jablanica, so nothing scenic is actually lost.
survivors.tradeoff: Loses the formal museum visit and the Battle-of-Neretva history context — a real loss for anyone in the group who is into WWII/Yugoslav history. Mitigated by keeping the free roadside view of the iconic sunken bridge. This is a committed (non-picked) stop, so confirm before cutting.

survivors.target: ba-boracko-lake (Boračko Lake swim stop, Day 6 dayOrder -1.0)
survivors.proposal: Replace the Boračko Lake mid-drive swim with a Bjelašnica-highland morning stop pulled from the pool: either the easy Studeni Potok waterfall walk from Umoljani (ba-studeni-potok-umoljani, ~1-1.5h, fully paved access) or the no-exposure Bjelašnica summit from Babin Do (ba-bjelasnica-summit-babindo, ~1.5-2h, paved resort road, 360° views). Both sit on the Konjic→Sarajevo line (~21km up from Konjic, ~26km back down to the Ilidža/Sarajevo approach) and deliver the 'meditation on a mountain / stargazing highland' the group explicitly wishlisted, plus the Rakitnica-canyon rim and Lukomir's stone-shingle shepherd village en route. This pairs naturally as the OTHER half of the day if the kayak (proposal 1) is done; or stands alone if the group skips the kayak. Do NOT drive the final 11km of gravel into Lukomir itself in the rental (clause risk) — Umoljani and Babin Do are paved; view Lukomir from the rim or the Umoljani side.
survivors.rationale: Boračko Lake is the day's weakest swim: it's a detour UP a hairpin road OFF the direct Konjic→Sarajevo line, and it duplicates water the Jablanica kayak already provides far better. The Bjelašnica highland is a rating-5 cluster that is genuinely on the Sarajevo approach corridor and gives the day a distinctive mountain/landscape highlight that contrasts with (rather than repeats) the water days around it (D5 swim/jump, D7 raft). It's a clean taste upgrade for the same drive-day slot.
survivors.tradeoff: Loses the easy lakeside swim and self-rent pedalo/rowboat at Boračko (a low-effort water break some of the group may prefer on a long drive day). The full Umoljani→Lukomir rim hike (6-7h) does NOT fit a Sarajevo-evening day — only the short walk or the easy summit do, so manage expectations on which Bjelašnica option. Slightly more driving than the lake detour. Boračko is a committed stop, so confirm before swapping.

survivors.target: Mratinje Dam (Piva dam) photo stop, D7 (dayOrder 2.5)
survivors.proposal: Add Vidikovac Babina Greda (pool id me-vidikovac-babina-greda-piva, 43.189364/18.8610641) as the canyon-view stop and demote Mratinje Dam to a 5-minute roll-by. Babina Greda is ~2.5km off the P14 at Donji Unač (paved drive-up, ~4km before Plužine, zero meaningful detour) and is repeatedly called Piva's most beautiful viewpoint, with COVERED shaded shelters + benches/tables over the turquoise reservoir and the Bioč-Maglić-Volujak + Durmitor wall.
survivors.rationale: The plan's own note calls Mratinje 'exposed concrete, no shade — don't linger' — it is a quick dam-wall photo, not a real view. Babina Greda delivers the actual canyon panorama from a shaded picnic shelter, which is exactly what a hot late-June afternoon (arriving ~15:00 after the cold rafting) wants. It also gives the day a proper sit-and-take-it-in highlight that isn't another water stop.
survivors.tradeoff: A few extra minutes for the 2.5km spur off the P14, and you skip lingering at the dam wall itself (still drive right past it, so a 5-min stop costs nothing). Minor: it's rating-3 / single strong source, so the 'most beautiful in Piva' billing is somewhat thinly sourced.

vet.target: Mratinje Dam (Piva dam) photo stop, D7 (dayOrder 2.5)
vet.reasoning:

survivors.target: Day 10 morning anchor near Rvaši base (pool id me-karuc-skadar)

Use it as the quiet bookend on EITHER fork — the headline if the group skips the far-south drive, or a pre-departure warm-up before the Murići serpentine.

survivors.tradeoff: Access is a narrow 2.5km road with tight curves 'in disrepair' (slow, careful drive) and parking is only ~8-10 cars — go early. survivors.target: Day 10 (Rvaši/Skadar 2-night base) — convert the second day from a Skadar-lake repeat into a sea-coast day; demote the D10 ★ Murići→Beška (me-murici-beska-swim)
survivors.proposal: Keep the booked N9-N10 Rvaši base (immovable), but change WHAT D10 does. As committed, D9 is a full Skadar day (Rijeka Crnojevića kayak + Danilo's-bridge swim + Pavlova Strana viewpoint) and D10 is ANOTHER full Skadar day (Murići→Beška boat-swim OR Virpazar SUP + Pješačac cove + winery sunset) — two consecutive lake-water days from the same bed, the trip's only landscape-repeat and a direct hit on the 'no same activity back-to-back' rule. Instead make D10 the trip's one Adriatic SEA day: Virpazar→Bar 0:30, Bar→Ulcinj 1:04. Anchor it on the open-sea coast the rest of the trip never touches — Velika Plaža / Ada Bojana (me-velika-plaza, me-ada-bojana — warm sandy shallows + kitesurf, a totally different water from lake/river/canyon), with Stari Bar fortress ruins (me-stari-bar) or Valdanos olive-grove cove (me-valdanos-bay-ulcinj) as the on-route add, and a stilt-restaurant seafood lunch on the Bojana (me-misko-stilt-restaurant). Then drive back to Rvaši for the night. Keep the Vinarija Mašanović winery sunset (me-vinarija-masanovic) as the optional D10 evening cap back near Virpazar if energy holds. Demote Murići→Beška from ★ to a backup option — its own note concedes it's '~1.5h single-lane serpentine EACH way' (a 3h round-trip drive for, again, a lake swim) the day after a full lake-kayak day.
survivors.rationale: This is the one change that most improves the whole trip because it fixes a STRUCTURAL flaw, not a single stop: the itinerary's only two-day landscape repeat. The plan already nails alpine (D8 Durmitor), canyon-raft (D7 Tara), river-canyon swims (D5 Drežnica), bay (D11 Kotor), and a lake-river day (D9 Skadar). The single missing ecosystem for an adventurous group is the OPEN ADRIATIC with warm sandy sea and kitesurf — and the post-pickup loop's only window for it is exactly here (the D3-4 island block ends Jun 19; Budva D11 is bay/cliff, not beach). Spending D10 on a second Skadar day burns a free, already-booked base on a repeat instead of cashing in the one sea-coast day the geography hands you for ~30-60 min of extra driving. It also upgrades the weakest committed ★ (a 3h serpentine round-trip for another lake swim) into a genuine highlight, and respects the back-to-back-activity rule the current D9/D10 pairing breaks.
survivors.tradeoff: Honest costs: (1) D10 adds ~1-1.5h driving vs a stay-local Skadar day (Bar 0:30 / Ulcinj ~1:04 each way), so it's a fuller day, not a rest day — though still lighter than the 3h Murići serpentine it replaces. (2) You give up the Murići/Beška island monasteries and the secret Pješačac cove (both genuinely nice) — but those are lake variants of water you already get a full day of on D9. (3) Ulcinj/Velika Plaža in late June can be busy and the far-south Adriatic is less 'hidden gem' than Skadar's coves; mitigate by leading with Ada Bojana/Valdanos rather than the main Ulcinj strip. (4) If the group is wiped after D7 raft / D8 Durmitor / D9 kayak, a quiet second Skadar day is the more restful choice — so this is mood-dependent, which is why D10 stays the flexible day of the pair.

vet.target: Day 10 (Rvaši/Skadar 2-night base) — convert the second day from a Skadar-lake repeat into a sea-coast day; demote the D10 ★ Murići→Beška (me-murici-beska-swim)
vet.reasoning: Strongest case AGAINST the change (and why it mostly wins): (1) The proposal's central premise is factually wrong. It claims D10 is "the post-pickup loop's only open-Adriatic window." It is not. The verified back-third is sea-saturated: D11 Budva = Sveti Nikola "Hawaii" OPEN-SEA cliff-jumping + Kotor-bay kayak; D12 Cavtat = self-drive boat + Rat-peninsula OPEN-Adriatic snorkel coves (a full sea day); D13 Dubrovnik = open-sea kayak Walls/Lokrum + Bellevue cliff-jump; plus D4 Mljet's Odysseus-Cave sea-cove jump. That is 3-4 open-Adriatic days already. The genuinely missing micro-ecosystem is narrowly "warm sand-bottom shallows + kitesurf," NOT "the open Adriatic" — a far weaker structural gap than the rationale asserts. (2) The drive math is anchored to the wrong point. The booked bed is at Rvaši on the NW shore, ~30 min NORTH of Virpazar (6.7km from D9's Rijeka Crnojevića, 14km from Virpazar). So the full Ada Bojana/Ulcinj day is ~3:10 round-trip from the actual bed (Rvaši→Virpazar 0:30 + Virpazar→Bar 0:30 + Bar→Ulcinj 0:34, doubled) — essentially the SAME ~3h driving the proposal condemns Murići for, just on tarmac, re-driving the Virpazar→Bar corridor twice and dumping the group back on the NW shore at night. It is not "+1-1.5h"; it is a full out-and-back transit day. And the one unique payoff (kitesurf) is verified CONDITIONAL — June thermals run lighter than midsummer, school has low-wind complaints — so 3h of driving can net a windless sand beach. (3) It demolishes a deliberately-designed rest day. The data is explicit that the D9-10 Rvaši 2-night base is "the only realistic wash window in 13 days of camping + saltwater — make D10 the rest + laundry day," landing right after D7 raft / D8 Durmitor summit / D9 kayak (three hard days). The rest-buffer rule says verbatim: do NOT re-pack the 2-night-base rest days. (4) The back-to-back concern is overstated: swims/SUP don't even count as "big highlights" under the user's rule, and D10 can simply be a chill lake rest day — it doesn't need a second paddle at all. WHY THE CHANGE STILL WINS (modified): the proposal correctly identifies two real weaknesses — the soft D9→D10 paddle repeat and a weak ★ (Murići = ~2.5h serpentine round-trip for yet another lake swim). The prior research already converged on the right fix, and it is NOT the kitesurf beach: the deep south's only verified must-do is Stari Bar (rating 5, the abandoned fortress town — a ruins category Montenegro otherwise lacks here) + the 2,240-yr Stara Maslina olive tree. A Stari Bar + Stara Maslina half-day is ~2h round-trip from Rvaši (vs ~3:10 for the full Ada run), gives D10 a genuine NON-water, non-repeat highlight (decisively fixing the back-to-back issue, far better than swapping kayak→sand-swim), and returns to base by afternoon for the rest/laundry window and the Mašanović winery sunset the proposal wanted to keep. This is the exact verdict the research already reached ("half-day Stari Bar dip = YES; full kitesurf day = no, June thermals unreliable, costs the base rest"). So: do NOT adopt the full Ada Bojana/Ulcinj sea-day swap (wrong premise on the "only sea window," understated 3h drive, gambles on conditional wind, kills the designated rest day). DO demote the Murići ★ as proposed, and replace it with the Stari Bar half-day already in the data — keeping D10 a light, base-anchored day with one real non-repeat highlight and slack preserved.

Make two targeted fixes the prior research already endorsed: (1) Demote the D10 ★ Murići→Beška (me-murici-beska-swim) from star to a backup option — its own note concedes a ~2.5h round-trip serpentine from the Rvaši NW-shore base for another warm-lake swim the day after a full lake-kayak day. The verified back-third is sea-saturated: D11 Budva = Sveti Nikola "Hawaii" OPEN-SEA cliff-jumping + Kotor-bay kayak; D12 Cavtat = self-drive boat + Rat-peninsula OPEN-Adriatic snorkel coves (a full sea day); D13 Dubrovnik = open-sea kayak Walls/Lokrum + Bellevue cliff-jump; plus D4 Mljet's Odysseus-Cave sea-cove jump. That is 3-4 open-Adriatic days already. The genuinely missing micro-ecosystem is narrowly "warm sand-bottom shallows + kitesurf," NOT "the open Adriatic" — a far weaker structural gap than the rationale asserts. (2) The drive math is anchored to the wrong point. The booked bed is at Rvaši on the NW shore, ~30 min NORTH of Virpazar (6.7km from D9's Rijeka Crnojevića, 14km from Virpazar). So the full Ada Bojana/Ulcinj day is ~3:10 round-trip from the actual bed (Rvaši→Virpazar 0:30 + Virpazar→Bar 0:30 + Bar→Ulcinj 0:34, doubled) — essentially the SAME ~3h driving the proposal condemns Murići for, just on tarmac, re-driving the Virpazar→Bar corridor twice and dumping the group back on the NW shore at night. It is not "+1-1.5h"; it is a full out-and-back transit day. And the one unique payoff (kitesurf) is verified CONDITIONAL — June thermals run lighter than midsummer, school has low-wind complaints — so 3h of driving can net a windless sand beach. (3) It demolishes a deliberately-designed rest day. The data is explicit that the D9-10 Rvaši 2-night base is "the only realistic wash window in 13 days of camping + saltwater — make D10 the rest + laundry day," landing right after D7 raft / D8 Durmitor summit / D9 kayak (three hard days). The rest-buffer rule says verbatim: do NOT re-pack the 2-night-base rest days. (4) The back-to-back concern is overstated: swims/SUP don't even count as "big highlights" under the user's rule, and D10 can simply be a chill lake rest day — it doesn't need a second paddle at all. WHY THE CHANGE STILL WINS (modified): the proposal correctly identifies two real weaknesses — the soft D9→D10 paddle repeat and a weak ★ (Murići = ~2.5h serpentine round-trip for yet another lake swim). The prior research already converged on the right fix, and it is NOT the kitesurf beach: the deep south's only verified must-do is Stari Bar (rating 5, the abandoned fortress town — a ruins category Montenegro otherwise lacks here) + the 2,240-yr Stara Maslina olive tree. A Stari Bar + Stara Maslina half-day is ~2h round-trip from Rvaši (vs ~3:10 for the full Ada run), gives D10 a genuine NON-water, non-repeat highlight (decisively fixing the back-to-back issue, far better than swapping kayak→sand-swim), and returns to base by afternoon for the rest/laundry window and the Mašanović winery sunset the proposal wanted to keep. This is the exact verdict the research already reached ("half-day Stari Bar dip = YES; full kitesurf day = no, June thermals unreliable, costs the base rest"). So: do NOT adopt the full Ada Bojana/Ulcinj sea-day swap (wrong premise on the "only sea window," understated 3h drive, gambles on conditional wind, kills the designated rest day). DO demote the Murići ★ as proposed, and replace it with the Stari Bar half-day already in the data — keeping D10 a light, base-anchored day with one real non-repeat highlight and slack preserved.

survivors.target: Battle of Neretva Museum & sunken bridge (ba-jablanica-neretva-museum), D6 dayOrder -2.0
survivors.proposal: Drop the museum from D6. Leaving Ravna, go straight to Boračko Lake (swim, already on the line) as the morning highlight, then push to Sarajevo. The sunken bridge is visible in ~60 seconds from the M-17 if anyone is curious — no need to stop or enter the museum.
survivors.rationale: This is a WWII history museum + monument — a direct taste violation (group dislikes museums/monuments unless iconic, and a Yugoslav-partisan museum is niche history, not iconic to them). D6 is the trip's longest clock (8-24): Jablanica->Sarajevo drive, Baščaršija evening, Žuta sunset, a bar crawl, then a ~40min dark drive to the Pale bed and a 07:30 D7 Tara start. Spending the scarce morning on a museum steals time from Boračko Lake (the day's only nature/swim beat) and from reaching Sarajevo rested.
survivors.tradeoff: You lose a genuinely photogenic, evocative WWII relic (the blown railway bridge in the Neretva gorge) and regional context some travelers rate highly. If anyone in the group is a history buff, this is the one they'd miss.

vet.target: Battle of Neretva Museum & sunken bridge (ba-jablanica-neretva-museum), D6 dayOrder -2.0
vet.reasoning:
Strongest case AGAINST the change (defending the current pin): The proposal's core premise — that the museum "steals the scarce morning from Boračko Lake" — is geographically false, and I verified it. Ravna/Blagaj (43.26,17.89) → Boračko Lake (43.55,18.03) has exactly one through-valley road: the M-17 up the Neretva. The sunken bridge + museum sits right where the M-17 hits Jablanica, BEFORE the Konjic turnoff to Boračko. You cannot reach the lake without passing it. So dropping it frees ~0 driving minutes — only the ~30 min standing-at-the-stop, which the place data's own consensus caps at "30 minutes is enough / a few minutes." On the no-back-to-back-activity rule, D6 is otherwise a town/nightlife day (Sarajevo Baščaršija, Žuta sunset, bar crawl) with Boračko as the lone nature/swim beat; the bridge is a different category (sight) that ADDS variety to a swim+town day rather than duplicating anything, and it's a textbook "we're tired → skip it, road rebuilds" item with literally zero detour penalty. The relic is free from the road and "hauntingly photogenic" per multiple sources — cheap value on a corridor you're driving anyway.

Why the change still partially wins: the proposal is RIGHT that the indoor Yugoslav-partisan WWII museum is a taste violation — the group dislikes non-iconic museums/monuments (per the "not into cities/museums" memory), and this is niche regional history, not iconic to them. They would not pay to walk the museum building. But the proposal overreaches by throwing out the free drive-by relic to "save" morning time the geography proves isn't saved. The proposal even concedes this by keeping the 60-second view. So the museum INTERIOR should go, the bridge STOP should stay. The place object already bundles both ("the bridge view is free from the road" + "small museum entry a few KM") — the right move is to keep the pin but reframe it as a quick free photo stop (a couple of minutes to stretch + shoot the wreck) on the way up to Boračko, not a committed museum visit. That preserves the photogenic WWII relic and a natural Jablanica lamb-lunch anchor at zero time cost, while honoring the taste rule by not committing to the indoor museum. Net: don't delete; demote scope from "museum visit" to "free bridge photo stop, museum optional."
